token-bonus.d: Extra token the target samples from its distribution at position \(k+1\) when all \(k\) drafts of a round are accepted. It comes for free, because that distribution was already computed in the verification forward. That's why a round emits up to \(k+1\) tokens.

num-lookahead-tokens.d: KV slots that vLLM's scheduler reserves per request, beyond the normal token, for a step's speculative positions (equal to \(k\) in EAGLE-, MTP- and DSpark-style proposers). Rejected rows are discarded and reused in the next round.

residuo-de-rejeicao.d: \( r(x) \propto \max(0,\,p(x)-q(x)) \): where the target samples the correction from when it rejects a draft. It contains only the tokens for which the target wanted more probability than the drafter offered, and it's what makes speculation lossless.

especulacao-sem-perdas.d: The guarantee that the emitted sequence has exactly the target model's distribution, whatever the drafter. It holds for standard rejection, with greedy or probabilistic drafting, up to numerical precision. It doesn't mean the same text: at \(T>0\), the same seed produces different text with the same distribution.

taxa-de-aceitacao.d: Probability that the target accepts a draft at a given position: \( \alpha = \sum_x \min(p(x), q(x)) = 1 - \mathrm{TV}(p,q) \). In /metrics it also shows up as a global fraction: accepted ÷ proposed drafts.

distancia-tv.d: \( \mathrm{TV}(p,q) = \tfrac12 \sum_x |p(x)-q(x)| \): the largest difference in probability that \(p\) and \(q\) can assign to the same event. In speculation, the chance of rejecting a draft is exactly \(\mathrm{TV}(p,q)\).

aceitacao-condicional.d: Probability \(c_i\) that draft position \(i\) is accepted given that all the previous ones were. The unconditional acceptance is the product \(a_i = \prod_{j\le i} c_j\).

aceitacao-por-posicao.d: Fraction \(a_i\) of steps in which the draft at position \(i\) and all the earlier ones were accepted. It's what the spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos counter divided by the number of drafts measures. It decays with \(i\) in a healthy recipe.

sobrevivencia-cumulativa.d: Probability that a draft prefix survives verification intact: the product of the conditional acceptances of its positions. It's the cumulative_survival function of the DSpark overlay and the basis for confidence-based length cutting.

tokens-por-passo.d: Tokens emitted per speculative decode step: 1 (bonus or correction) + accepted drafts, or \( \tau = 1 + \sum_i a_i \). With independent, constant acceptance α, \( \tau(k) = (1-\alpha^{k+1})/(1-\alpha) \), which tends to \(1/(1-\alpha)\).

draft-sample-method.d: --speculative-config field that defines how the drafter picks its token. greedy (vLLM's default): argmax, with \(q\) treated as one-hot, acceptance \(p(\hat x)\). probabilistic: samples from \(q\) and stores the full distribution, acceptance \(1-\mathrm{TV}\), at a memory cost. Both are lossless.

rejection-sample-method.d: --speculative-config field with the verification rule. standard: accepts with \(\min(1,p/q)\) and resamples from the residual, lossless. synthetic: prescribed acceptance rates, doesn't preserve the target's distribution and is only good for benchmarking. v0.30 added block, block verification, also lossless.

verificacao-greedy.d: Special case of rejection sampling when the request is greedy (\(T=0\)): the target accepts the draft if it's its own argmax. In vLLM, this is the rejection_greedy_sample_kernel.

prompt-lookup.d: Drafter with no neural network (method: ngram): it looks up the last \(n\) generated tokens in the context itself and proposes as the draft what came after them (prompt_lookup_min/max). Near-zero cost; pays off in code editing, RAG and summarization.

suffix-decoding.d: Drafter with no neural network (method: suffix) that maintains a suffix tree of the prompt and of previous responses and proposes the most frequent continuation. Suited to repetitive traffic, such as agents that resend the same snippets.

modelo-rascunho.d: A small, standalone LM used as the drafter (method: draft_model). It needs the same tokenizer as the target (or use_heterogeneous_vocab), has its own KV and costs \(k\) back-to-back forwards per step.

snapshot-de-estado.d: Copies of the recurrent state (SSM/linear attention) and of the short convolution's window saved after each of the \(k+1\) verification tokens. After the verdict, the snapshot matching the accepted tokens becomes the official state. It's the exact, cheap rollback: inverting the updates would be unstable in floating point, and the conv has already dropped its old columns.

num-accepted-tokens.d: Per-request tensor that vLLM passes to the state kernels (Mamba, GDN, KDA, short conv) after verification: how many of the step's tokens counted. It picks which state snapshot becomes the official one and how far the conv window rewinds (num_accepted_tokens − 1).

spec-accept-gate.d: GLM's post-boot check, run by hand (start.sh doesn't call it): it reads /metrics and, with ≥ 100 drafts, fails if the position-0 ratio goes above 0.999 (PASS if ≤ 0.999; SKIP below 100 drafts; exit 2 if it can't judge). It only judges position 0 and prints the rest. It detects vllm#53030, a BatchDescriptor collision in PIECEWISE graphs that pins acceptance at 1.00.

metricas-spec-decode.d: vLLM's Prometheus counters: vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total (proposals), num_draft_tokens_total (drafts), num_accepted_tokens_total and num_accepted_tokens_per_pos_total{position=…}. They are cumulative since boot and must be read by delta.

regra-de-parada-fcost.d: TensorFold depth policy (fcostN:noisy): each round, it walks the whole draft chain and cuts it at the \(k\) that maximizes \(E[\text{tokens}\mid k]/\text{ms}(k)\), using the chain's predicted confidences and a cost table measured at startup. It is speculation's marginal rule applied round by round; the GLM·TF recipe defaults to fnc7:0.3.

simulador-de-rascunhos.d: TensorFold tool (patch 0011): with TF_GLM_DRAFT_DUMP, the request decodes one token per round and records what DFlash2 would have proposed at each position and the committed token; a NumPy program then replays any stop rule's rounds exactly and turns them into tok/s with a cost table. It is only exact because sampling is keyed.

alocacao-conjunta.d: Optional TensorFold mode (TF_GLM_MULTI_DEPTH=joint) that splits a round's verification rows among the streams: each row goes to the draft with the highest predicted chance of surviving, as long as expected tokens per millisecond keep growing. The GLM·TF recipe stays on the default policy.

commit-tardio.d: After a partial acceptance, instead of replaying the recurrent state right away, keep the inputs of the accepted rows and apply them at the start of the next forward pass. It removes the replay pass and, in Nemotron-3.5-Bolt (SSM_LAZY=1), the second copy of the state: 0.41 → 0.28 GiB per stream, with the same bits.
